newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: German, Austrian kidnap victims killed in Colombia.
newsitem.headline: German, Austrian kidnap victims killed in Colombia.

text.p: Two kidnapped foreign tourists from Germany and Austria were killed on Tuesday when army troops raided a guerrilla encampment in northwest Colombia where they had been held captive for a month, military officials said.

Two other German and Austrian citizens were freed in the raid and four leftist Revolutionary Armed Forces of Colombia (FARC) rebels were killed, Gen. Ivan Ramirez, a regional military commander, told Reuters.

He identified the dead, who he said were killed by rebels when soldiers raided the camp in a jungle-covered area of northwestern Choco province, as Alexander Scheurer of Germany and Johann Kehrer of Austria.
Kehrer's brother, Manfred, was rescued along with Mardean Muzinic of Germany, Ramirez said.
Defence Minister Guillermo Alberto Gonzalez told a news conference that two U.S. citizens were freed in the raid on the camp, but Ramirez insisted that no Americans were involved.
"They were tourists who entered from Panama," Ramirez said in a telephone interview, adding that the Germans and Austrians had entered Colombia on Feb. 5 to visit the Los Catios nature reserve.
They were seized by FARC rebels two days later, he said.
German and Austrian embassy officials could not be reached for immediate comment on the identity or hometowns of the victims or the circumstances under which they were killed.
The FARC, Colombia's largest and oldest rebel group, specialises in kidnappings and the protection of rural drug operations.
